page.layout: One printed page, numbered 448, with a running head at the top. Its main text is one column of running text with paragraph numbers 25, 26 and 27 in the left margin. A catchword sits at the lower right. A partial page from the neighbouring leaf shows at the right edge and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: lent deos alienos. Propterea irascetur furor Je-hovæ in vos,& disperdet te cito. Deut.7.v.3.

25. Si tamen ad bellum contra inimicos tuos egressus, captivos ex eis abduxeris, videris autem in captivitate mulierem pulchram formâ, & deamaveris eam, & acceperis tibi in uxorem: introducito eam domum tuam, & radito ipsa caput suum, ac crescere facito ungues suos, deponitoq; vestimentum captivitatis suæ à se, & maneto in domo tua, ac fleto patrem suum, & matrem suam mensem integrum: & postea ingreditor ad eam, estoq; maritus ejus, & esto tibi uxor. Deut.21.v.10.

26. Si postea non complacueris tibi in ea, tum dimittito eam animæ suæ, (id est, liberam, ut abeat, quocunque libuerit) nec vendendo ven-dito eam pecuniâ, neque negociator de ea, quòd afflixeris eam. Deut.21.v.14.

27. Cùm fuerint viro duæ uxores, una dilecta, & altera exosa, & pepererint ei filios, dilecta, & exosa; fuerit autem filius primogenitus exosæ: die, quo hæredes instituet filios suos, eorum, quæ habuerit, non poterit dare jus primogenituræ filio dilectæ, ante filium exosæ primogenitum: sed primogenitum filium exosæ agnoscito, ut det ei mensuram duorum ex omnibus, quæ habuerit. Ipse enim est principium fortitudinis ejus, ipsius est jus primogenituræ. Deut.21.v.51[?].

page.notes: The right edge shows part of the neighbouring page with text fragments; this is not transcribed. The reference "Deut.21.v.51" at the end of paragraph 27 is doubtful; Deuteronomy 21:17 would be expected, so the printed numeral may be 17 and is uncertain from the scan. The word "estoq;" in paragraph 25 is hard to read and is only approximate. The running head "Libri IV." is in small capitals.
